intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass
experiences.description: Ski the world-famous slopes of Zermatt with stunning views of the Matterhorn. With over 360km of marked runs, this resort caters to all skill levels. Book slopes near the village base to maximize time after a late Day 1 arrival, starting fresh on Day 2. Stay in Zermatt village to walk to lifts each morning.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Explore the breathtaking Jungfrau region on guided snowshoe trails through pristine alpine landscapes. Trails depart directly from Grindelwald village center, making it ideal for those staying locally. A perfect mid-week activity after ski days, requiring no special equipment rental beyond snowshoes included in the tour.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz and optionally ride the historic Olympia Bob Run, one of the world's oldest natural ice bobsled tracks. Both attractions are within walking distance of St. Moritz village center, eliminating transfer time. Best enjoyed mid-afternoon when ice conditions are optimal.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening
experiences.description: Join a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner experience in a historic mountain chalet in Verbier village. Learn about centuries-old Alpine cheese-making culture while warming up after a day on the slopes. Restaurants are clustered in the village center, perfect for guests staying in Verbier accommodations.

experiences.name: Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure
experiences.description: Ride the iconic cable car to Glacier 3000 above Les Diablerets for panoramic views across four countries. Experience the Snow Bus ride across the glacier plateau and visit the Peak Walk suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks. The base station is a short walk from Les Diablerets village, ideal for a full afternoon excursion on a rest day from skiing.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport, take a regional train or bus toward Poschiavo via the Bernina Express route. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle in, unpack, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport or train station (sandwiches, pretzels, or a kebab wrap for ~CHF 8-12). Alternatively, pick up snacks at a Migros or Coop convenience store en route.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express from Chur to Tirano passes through Poschiavo — a scenic and budget-friendly rail option. Book tickets in advance via SBB.ch for the best fares. The B&B is located in the quiet village of Poschiavo in the Graubünden canton. Confirm late check-in with the host before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty B&B breakfast, take a short walk around the charming village of Poschiavo. Explore the historic Piazza Comunale, admire the Spanish-style houses, and visit the Church of San Vittore. The village is compact and walkable — a perfect gentle start to the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Diavolezza ski area (~45 min by Bernina Express train to Pontresina/Diavolezza station). Purchase a day ski pass (budget tip: check for online early-bird deals, ~CHF 55-65/day). Enjoy beginner to intermediate ski runs with stunning views of the Morteratsch Glacier and Piz Palü.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Stroll along the village streets in the crisp mountain air. Warm up with a hot chocolate or Glühwein at a local café.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich from the B&B or grab a budget mountain lunch at the Diavolezza mountain restaurant (soup + bread ~CHF 12-15). Alternatively, bring your own thermos of soup.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Croce Federale in Poschiavo — a local trattoria offering hearty Graubünden dishes like pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) and polenta for ~CHF 18-25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rent ski equipment in Poschiavo or at the Diavolezza base station to save money vs. resort rental shops. Bring your own snacks and water to avoid expensive on-mountain prices. Bernina Express day pass or regional rail ticket covers the train to Diavolezza station.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express train to St. Moritz (~40 min, ~CHF 10-12 one way). Explore the famous resort town on foot — window shop on Via Serlas, admire the frozen Lake St. Moritz, and enjoy the glamorous atmosphere without spending a fortune.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Corviglia ski area above St. Moritz (funicular from town center). Ski or snowboard on well-groomed intermediate runs with panoramic Engadin valley views. A half-day ski pass (afternoon) costs ~CHF 40-50, saving money vs. a full-day pass.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Relax at the B&B. Optional: join other guests for conversation or play cards in the common area.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Pick up a budget lunch from a Migros or Coop supermarket in St. Moritz (sandwiches, yogurt, fruit ~CHF 8-10) and eat by the frozen lake.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from the local Poschiavo shop (pasta, local cheese, cured meats ~CHF 10-12 total). Many B&Bs allow use of a small kitchen — confirm with host.

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of the world's most expensive ski resorts, but visiting on a budget is possible by using public transport, buying supermarket food, and opting for a half-day ski pass. The Bernina railway is a UNESCO World Heritage route — enjoy the scenery!

day_by_day.morning: Try snowshoeing directly from Poschiavo — rent snowshoes locally (~CHF 15-20/day) and explore the snow-covered trails around the Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo). The flat lakeside trail is easy and incredibly scenic with mountain reflections on the frozen lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snowshoeing or switch to a self-guided winter hiking trail toward the Alp Grüm viewpoint (accessible by Bernina Express train, ~CHF 6). Alp Grüm offers breathtaking views of the Palü Glacier and the Italian Alps — one of the most dramatic viewpoints in the region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo. Visit the local Museo di Poschiavo (small entry fee ~CHF 5) to learn about the valley's unique Italian-Swiss culture and history.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch — buy local bread, Bündner Fleisch (air-dried beef), and cheese from the village shop (~CHF 10-12). Eat with a view at Alp Grüm.
meals.dinner: Pizzeria/Trattoria Al Cervo in Poschiavo — wood-fired pizza and pasta dishes for ~CHF 15-22 per person. A local favorite with generous portions.

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoeing is one of the most budget-friendly winter activities in the Alps — no lift pass required! The Lago di Poschiavo trail is approximately 8 km round trip and suitable for all fitness levels. Dress in warm layers and waterproof boots.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express to Pontresina (~35 min). Pontresina is a quieter, more affordable alternative to St. Moritz. Explore the village, visit the Santa Maria Chapel with its medieval frescoes, and browse the local ski shops for any gear needs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski at Lagalb ski area near Pontresina/Diavolezza — a less crowded, more affordable alternative to Corviglia. Lagalb is known for challenging off-piste terrain and stunning views. Day pass ~CHF 55. Alternatively, try cross-country skiing (Langlauf) on the Engadin valley trails — a very budget-friendly option (~CHF 15-20 for trail pass + rental).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo. Treat yourself to a relaxing evening — take a warm bath, read, or enjoy a glass of local Valposchiavo wine from the B&B or a nearby shop.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Grab a Wurst (sausage) and bread from a mountain snack hut (~CHF 8-10) or bring your own packed lunch.
meals.dinner: Osteria della Posta in Poschiavo — a cozy local osteria serving traditional Graubünden cuisine including maluns (potato dish) and venison stew for ~CHF 20-28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country skiing in the Engadin valley is world-class and significantly cheaper than downhill skiing. The Engadin Skimarathon route passes through this area — trails are perfectly groomed in February. Pontresina is also a great base for ice climbing and winter mountaineering if interested.

day_by_day.morning: Full ski day at Diavolezza — make the most of your skills developed during the week. Try the famous Diavolezza glacier run (12 km off-piste descent to Morteratsch) — one of the most spectacular ski descents in the Alps. This requires intermediate-advanced skills and ideally a guide for first-timers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza or take a break to visit the Morteratsch Glacier on foot. The glacier trail from Morteratsch station is free and offers an awe-inspiring close-up view of the retreating glacier with historical marker posts showing its recession over decades.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a celebratory final full-day dinner. Explore the village one last time under the stars — the dark skies around Poschiavo offer incredible stargazing opportunities in winter.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain restaurant at Diavolezza — choose the daily special (Tagesmenü) for the best value (~CHF 16-20 including soup and main).
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full evening — Ristorante Croce Federale or Hotel Albrici restaurant in Poschiavo for a 2-course meal with local wine (~CHF 30-38 per person). A well-deserved treat!

day_by_day.notes: Saturday tends to be busier on the slopes — arrive at Diavolezza early (before 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and get first tracks on the glacier. The Morteratsch Glacier walk is free and takes about 1.5 hours round trip — highly recommended even for non-skiers.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast at the B&B. Take a slow morning walk around Poschiavo village, pick up local souvenirs — Bündner Nusstorte (nut tart), local honey, or Graubünden wine from the village shop at very reasonable prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, take one final scenic ride on the Bernina Express toward Chur or toward Tirano (Italy side) for a short cross-border excursion (~CHF 15 round trip). The Bernina Pass views in winter are absolutely stunning. Return to Poschiavo, collect luggage, and begin journey to departure airport.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Zurich Airport or Milan Malpensa for onward flight. The train journey from Poschiavo to Zurich takes approximately 3.5-4 hours via Chur. Book tickets in advance on SBB.ch for best prices.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — enjoy a final Swiss breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pick up a Migros or Coop meal deal at the train station (~CHF 8-12) for an affordable and convenient travel lunch.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or train station food court — budget for ~CHF 15-20 or bring snacks from the village.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at the B&B is typically 10:00-11:00 AM — confirm with host. Store luggage at the B&B if needed for a morning activity. The Bernina Express is a bucket-list train journey — even a short segment is worth it. Book SBB tickets 1-2 days in advance for the best fares. Total estimated daily budget: CHF 80-120/day including ski passes, meals, and transport (excluding accommodation).

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Check in, settle into your room, and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama around midnight. If the kitchen is closed, grab a light snack from any provisions brought along or ask the host about late-night options. Unpack and get a good night's sleep to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light snack at the B&B or airport meal before departure. Consider picking up a sandwich or pastry at Zurich/Geneva airport before the final leg of your journey.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at 22:30. No sightseeing or activities planned. Confirm your transfer to Poschiavo in advance — the village is in the Graubünden canton and may require a pre-booked taxi or shuttle from the nearest rail hub (Tirano or Pontresina). Journey time from Zurich Airport is approximately 3–4 hours by train + bus or 2.5 hours by car.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely B&B breakfast and take a gentle orientation walk around the charming village of Poschiavo. Explore the historic Piazza Comunale, admire the Romanesque church, and soak in the stunning Bernina mountain backdrop. This is a relaxed start to ease into alpine life after your late arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Livigno or Diavolezza ski area (both accessible from Poschiavo via the Bernina Pass road or train). Diavolezza is approximately 30–40 minutes away and offers excellent intermediate skiing with jaw-dropping views of the Bernina massif and Morteratsch Glacier. Rent ski equipment at the base station if needed and enjoy a half-day on the slopes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a relaxed evening. Stroll along Via Principale and explore the local shops. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant in the village.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — expect fresh bread, cold cuts, cheese, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant at Diavolezza ski area — try a hearty Rösti with cheese or a warm soup. Budget CHF 20–30.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse or a local trattoria in Poschiavo — enjoy regional Graubünden specialties like Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables) or Capuns. Budget CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza ski area is part of the Engadin St. Moritz ski region. A day ski pass costs approximately CHF 65–75. Equipment rental is available at the base. Check snow conditions and lift status the morning of. Poschiavo has a strong Italian-Swiss cultural influence — menus may be in Italian.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to St. Moritz — approximately 45 minutes from Poschiavo by the scenic Bernina Express train or by car over the Bernina Pass. Begin your morning with the St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience: lace up your skates and glide across the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz, one of the most iconic winter settings in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, take on the historic Olympia Bob Run — one of the oldest and most famous bobsled tracks in the world, dating back to 1904. Guests can ride as a passenger with a professional pilot for an unforgettable adrenaline rush. Alternatively, explore the upscale village of St. Moritz, browse the boutiques on Via Serlas, or visit the Segantini Museum for alpine art.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner back in the village or pick up local provisions for a cozy in-room meal.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Café or bistro in St. Moritz — try Café Hauser or a local bakery for a mid-range lunch. Expect CHF 25–40 for a meal. St. Moritz can be pricey — opt for lunch menus (Tagesmenü) for better value.
meals.dinner: Osteria Poschiavina or similar local eatery in Poschiavo — try local Graubünden sausages, polenta, or a simple pasta dish. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express train from Poschiavo to St. Moritz is a UNESCO World Heritage route and a scenic highlight in itself — book tickets in advance via SBB (Swiss Federal Railways). The bobsled experience costs approximately CHF 150–200 per person. Ice skating on Lake St. Moritz is weather-dependent — confirm the lake is frozen and open to the public before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Today is dedicated to the Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass experience. Depart early from Poschiavo — Zermatt is approximately 2.5–3 hours by train (via Chur or St. Moritz and Visp). Arrive in Zermatt (a car-free village) and head straight to the lifts. Begin skiing the world-famous slopes with breathtaking views of the iconic Matterhorn. Over 360km of marked runs cater to all skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing through the afternoon on Zermatt's varied terrain — from the Rothorn and Stockhorn areas for intermediates to the Klein Matterhorn (Matterhorn Glacier Paradise) for high-altitude runs. Take a break at one of the mountain restaurants to refuel and admire the panoramic alpine scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zermatt village in the early evening — browse the charming pedestrian streets, visit the Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis), and enjoy dinner before catching the train back to Poschiavo. Note: return journey is long — consider an overnight stay in Zermatt if budget allows, or plan for a late return.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast or grab a pastry and coffee at Poschiavo train station before departure.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on the Zermatt slopes — try Chez Vrony or Blauherd restaurant for stunning Matterhorn views. Budget CHF 30–45 for a mountain lunch.
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Zermatt village before your return train — try Walliserkanne for traditional Valais fondue and raclette. Budget CHF 40–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: A Zermatt full-day ski pass costs approximately CHF 85–95. Book train tickets in advance via SBB — the journey involves multiple connections. Zermatt is car-free; electric taxis and horse-drawn carriages operate in the village. Given the long travel day, consider whether an overnight stay in Zermatt (budget hotel ~CHF 120–160/night) makes more sense than a same-day return to Poschiavo.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and local exploration day. After the big Zermatt excursion, enjoy a slower morning. Have a leisurely B&B breakfast and then explore the Poschiavo Valley on a gentle winter walk along the valley floor. The Val Poschiavo offers beautiful scenery with snow-covered meadows, frozen streams, and views of the surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Jungfrau Region for the Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience. Travel to Grindelwald or Wengen (approximately 2.5–3 hours by train via Chur and Interlaken). Join a guided snowshoe tour through pristine alpine landscapes, exploring trails that wind through snow-laden forests and open alpine meadows with stunning views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the B&B or a nearby restaurant. This is a good evening to reflect on the week and plan any last-minute activities.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast at Berninahaus Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or mountain hut refreshments during the snowshoe tour — many guided tours include a warm drink and snack stop at a mountain hut. Budget CHF 15–25.
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant — try a warming Minestrone soup followed by Brasato (braised beef) or a cheese plate with local Graubünden specialties. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Guided snowshoe tours in the Jungfrau region typically cost CHF 50–80 per person including equipment rental. Book in advance through Jungfrau Region tourism or local guide services. The Jungfrau region is a long day trip from Poschiavo — consider whether to split this into a shorter local snowshoe alternative near Pontresina or Diavolezza to reduce travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure. Travel to Les Diablerets in the Vaud Alps (approximately 3–3.5 hours from Poschiavo by train via Bern or Lausanne). Ride the iconic cable car to Glacier 3000 at 3,000 meters above sea level for panoramic views spanning four countries — Switzerland, France, Italy, and Germany. Walk across the Peak Walk suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience the Snow Bus — a unique ride across the glacier on a specially designed snow vehicle. Enjoy skiing or snowboarding on the glacier slopes, or try the alpine coaster and snow tubing for family-friendly fun. Take time to simply absorb the extraordinary high-altitude glacier environment.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Poschiavo. Enjoy your final full evening with the Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening — join a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner in a historic mountain chalet setting (book in advance in Verbier or a nearby village, or arrange a similar fondue experience locally in Poschiavo or Pontresina).

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before early departure.
meals.lunch: Restaurant at Glacier 3000 summit — enjoy a meal with extraordinary views. The Botta 3000 restaurant offers mid-range dining. Budget CHF 30–45.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening — traditional fondue (moitié-moitié with Gruyère and Vacherin), raclette, and local wines in a historic chalet setting. Budget CHF 55–75 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 cable car tickets cost approximately CHF 45–55 return. The Snow Bus experience is an additional CHF 10–15. Book the fondue cultural evening in advance — if the Verbier experience is too far, arrange a similar fondue dinner at a local Poschiavo or Pontresina restaurant. Saturday can be busy at popular ski resorts — arrive early at Glacier 3000 to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely last B&B breakfast and take a final walk around Poschiavo village. Visit the local Sunday market if available, pick up Swiss souvenirs — local cheeses, chocolates, Graubünden dried meats (Bündnerfleisch), or a bottle of local Poschiavo wine. Pack your bags and check out of the B&B.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy one last activity — a short ski run at Diavolezza, a scenic ride on the Bernina Express toward Tirano (Italy) and back, or simply a peaceful walk along the lake in St. Moritz. Begin your transfer to the airport (Zurich ~3.5 hours, Milan Malpensa ~2.5 hours) in the early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Airport transfer and departure. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, winter sports, and alpine adventures in one of the world's most beautiful mountain destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final full B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — savor the last Swiss breakfast spread.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Poschiavo or St. Moritz before departure — try a Capuns wrap or a Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart) as a farewell Swiss treat. Budget CHF 15–25.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your checkout time with the B&B host. Arrange your airport transfer in advance — Poschiavo is relatively remote and taxis should be pre-booked. The Bernina Express to Tirano (Italy) connects to Milan by train, making Milan Malpensa a viable departure airport. Alternatively, travel north via Pontresina and Chur to Zurich Airport. Allow ample travel time given the mountain terrain and potential winter road conditions.

A truly once-in-a-lifetime winter sports experience.
day_by_day.afternoon_detail: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience — full afternoon block (approx. 13:00–17:00).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a top-tier St. Moritz restaurant before returning to Poschiavo. Explore the glamorous St. Moritz village, browse luxury boutiques on Via Serlas, and soak in the atmosphere of the world's most famous winter resort.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — fresh local pastries, regional cheeses, cold cuts, eggs, fruit, and premium Swiss coffee or tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mathis Food Affairs (St. Moritz) — a beloved alpine institution offering refined Swiss and international cuisine with stunning Engadin valley views. Reservation recommended.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Acla da Fans or La Marmite in St. Moritz — both offer exceptional alpine fine dining with seasonal menus featuring local Graubünden ingredients, truffles, and an extensive Swiss wine list. Private transfer back to Poschiavo after dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Olympia Bob Run experience well in advance — slots fill quickly, especially on weekends. The Bob Run operates on select days; confirm availability for February 16. Wear warm, windproof layers for both ice skating and the bobsled. Private transfer between Poschiavo and St. Moritz is recommended for comfort and flexibility — the Bernina Express train is also a scenic luxury option if timed correctly.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, depart early for Zermatt via private luxury transfer (approximately 3–3.5 hours from Poschiavo, passing through stunning Engadin and Valais landscapes). Arrive in Zermatt — a car-free alpine paradise — and check your ski equipment into a premium rental shop such as Slalom Sport or Bayard Sport for top-of-the-line gear fitting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass experience. With over 360km of marked runs across three countries (Switzerland, Italy, and France), Zermatt offers world-class skiing for all levels. Spend the afternoon carving pristine pistes with the iconic Matterhorn as your backdrop. Take the Klein Matterhorn cable car to Europe's highest ski area at 3,883m for breathtaking panoramic views and exceptional high-altitude runs.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski in Zermatt village — visit the legendary Hennu Stall or Papperla Pub for a celebratory Glühwein. Stroll the charming car-free village streets before a gourmet dinner. Overnight in Zermatt (upgrade recommended — book a luxury hotel for this night to avoid the long return transfer).

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama before departure.
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Chez Vrony — Zermatt's most celebrated mountain restaurant, perched at 2,000m with direct Matterhorn views. Famous for its Valais beef, local cheeses, and exceptional wine list. Reservation essential.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Zum See — a legendary Zermatt institution set in a 400-year-old farmhouse in the forest. Exceptional seasonal alpine cuisine, intimate atmosphere, and an award-winning wine cellar. One of Switzerland's most iconic dining experiences. Reservation essential months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — arrange a private electric taxi from Täsch (the last car-accessible village) into Zermatt. Book ski passes online in advance to avoid queues. Consider hiring a private ski guide for the day to access the best runs and hidden powder stashes. If overnighting in Zermatt, the Mont Cervin Palace or The Omnia are exceptional luxury options. Confirm ski conditions and lift status before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Full second day of skiing at Zermatt Ski Resort. Start early to catch the best morning snow conditions on the high-altitude runs. Take the Gornergrat Bahn — a historic cogwheel railway — for a spectacular sunrise view over the Monte Rosa massif and 29 surrounding peaks above 4,000m. Begin skiing from the top for an unforgettable morning descent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Italian side of the Zermatt ski area — ski over the border to Cervinia, Italy, for a change of scenery and a taste of Italian alpine culture. The cross-border skiing experience is one of Zermatt's most unique offerings. Wider, gentler slopes on the Italian side are perfect for a relaxed afternoon cruise.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zermatt village for a final evening of luxury. Visit the Matterhorn Museum (Zermatlantis) for a fascinating cultural insight into the history of alpine mountaineering. Enjoy a farewell Zermatt dinner before private transfer back to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast in Zermatt (if overnighting) — or a café breakfast at Café du Pont in the village.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rifugio Guide del Cervino on the Italian side — a rustic mountain hut serving authentic Italian alpine cuisine: fresh pasta, risotto, and local Aosta Valley wines. A delightful cross-cultural experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Capri Restaurant at the Mont Cervin Palace Hotel — refined Mediterranean and Swiss cuisine in an elegant Belle Époque setting. Exceptional wine list and impeccable service. Private transfer back to Poschiavo after dinner (approximately 3.5 hours).

day_by_day.notes: A cross-border ski pass (Zermatt + Cervinia) must be purchased — confirm this is included in your Full-Day Pass or upgrade accordingly. Bring your passport for the Italian border crossing. The return transfer to Poschiavo will be a late evening drive — arrange a professional private driver in advance. Alternatively, consider one more night in Zermatt and return to Poschiavo on Day 5 morning.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at B&B Berninahaus Poschiavo Panorama after the Zermatt adventure. Enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast with valley views. Take a gentle morning stroll through Poschiavo's historic old town — visit the Collegiate Church of San Vittore and the charming Romansh-influenced piazzas. Browse local artisan shops for Swiss chocolates, regional spirits, and handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for the Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure near Les Diablerets (approximately 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo via private transfer). Ride the iconic cable car to Glacier 3000 at 3,000m elevation for jaw-dropping panoramic views across four countries — Switzerland, France, Italy, and Germany. Experience the thrilling Snow Bus ride across the glacier plateau and walk across the Peak Walk suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks — a world first.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey toward Poschiavo with a scenic stop in the Vaud Alps region. Enjoy a sunset aperitif at a mountain viewpoint before the drive back. Arrive at the B&B for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — take your time and enjoy the mountain panorama.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Botta 3000 at Glacier 3000 — a striking contemporary restaurant designed by architect Mario Botta, offering refined alpine cuisine at 3,000m elevation. Exceptional views and a sophisticated menu featuring Swiss seasonal ingredients.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — a beloved local institution serving traditional Graubünden and Italian-influenced cuisine reflecting the valley's unique cultural blend. Try the pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta), capretto (roasted kid goat), and local Poschiavo valley wines.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 is located above Les Diablerets in the canton of Vaud — it is a longer day trip from Poschiavo but absolutely worth it for the unique glacier experience. Book cable car tickets and Snow Bus in advance. The Peak Walk bridge is weather-dependent — check conditions. Wear very warm layers at 3,000m; temperatures can be extreme in February. Consider hiring a private driver for the full day to maximize comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Depart after breakfast for the Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience (approximately 2–2.5 hours from Poschiavo via private transfer to Grindelwald or Wengen). Meet your expert guide for a private guided snowshoe tour through the pristine Jungfrau alpine landscape — one of Switzerland's most spectacular UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Trek through snow-laden forests, across frozen meadows, and up to breathtaking viewpoints overlooking the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau triumvirate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoe experience or transition to a scenic winter hike on groomed trails above Grindelwald. Visit the Grindelwald First viewpoint for panoramic Bernese Oberland vistas. Optional: try the First Cliff Walk — a thrilling cliff-side walkway with glass-floored viewing platforms suspended above the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Grindelwald village for a celebratory dinner before the return transfer to Poschiavo. Explore the charming village atmosphere and browse local alpine craft shops.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama before departure.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by your guide on the snowshoe trail — a curated alpine picnic with local cheeses, cured meats, artisan bread, hot soup in a thermos, and Swiss chocolate. A magical experience in the heart of the Jungfrau wilderness.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Schmitte in Grindelwald — a charming historic restaurant in a converted blacksmith's forge, serving exceptional Bernese Oberland cuisine: Berner Platte, alpine cheese dishes, and locally sourced meats. Warm, rustic atmosphere perfect for a post-adventure celebration.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private guided snowshoe tour in advance through a certified Jungfrau region guide service. Snowshoes and poles are typically provided — confirm with your guide. Wear waterproof, insulated boots and layered clothing. The First Cliff Walk requires a separate gondola ticket — book online. Return transfer to Poschiavo will be approximately 2–2.5 hours; plan dinner timing accordingly to allow a comfortable evening return.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — savor a long, leisurely gourmet breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama with panoramic valley views. Pack and prepare for departure. Take a final short walk to the Bernina Pass viewpoint (just above the village) for one last breathtaking panorama of the Rhaetian Alps — a perfect farewell to the mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening (scheduled as an afternoon farewell experience if departing late, or enjoy as a final lunch experience). Join a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette experience in a historic mountain chalet setting — a quintessential Swiss cultural immersion. Learn about the centuries-old traditions of Swiss alpine cheese-making while enjoying a convivial, warming meal. Alternatively, spend the afternoon exploring the Poschiavo valley — visit the Lago di Poschiavo lakeside promenade and the historic Brusio Circular Viaduct (a UNESCO World Heritage Rhaetian Railway landmark).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Poschiavo via private luxury transfer to your departure airport (Zurich or Milan Malpensa). Reflect on an extraordinary week of world-class skiing, glacier adventures, snowshoeing, and Swiss alpine culture. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — request a special spread from your host: local honey, homemade jams, regional cheeses, fresh pastries, and premium coffee. Savor every moment.
meals.lunch: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Experience — a festive, communal farewell meal featuring traditional Gruyère and Vacherin fondue, raclette, charcuterie, cornichons, and local Graubünden white wine. The ultimate Swiss alpine send-off.
meals.dinner: Airport or en-route dining — if departing via Zurich, consider a final dinner at Clouds Restaurant in the Prime Tower (Zurich) for panoramic city views and refined Swiss-international cuisine, or dine at the airport's Marché Movenpick for quality Swiss fare before your flight.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and calculate transfer time carefully — Poschiavo to Zurich Airport is approximately 2.5–3 hours; to Milan Malpensa approximately 2 hours. Allow extra buffer time for Sunday traffic and winter road conditions. The Bernina Pass road may have restrictions in severe winter weather — confirm road status with your transfer driver. Purchase last-minute Swiss souvenirs in Poschiavo: local Bernina Grappa, Poschiavo valley honey, Swiss chocolate, and Rhaetian Railway memorabilia. Tip your B&B hosts generously — their local knowledge and hospitality will have been invaluable throughout your stay.
